domain: CNC Milling Machine Spindle & Process Fault Diagnosis
description: Comprehensive rule-based system integrating operator heuristic observations with real-time physical telemetry (AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance Dataset)

equipment.name: CNC Vertical Machining Center
sub_components: Spindle Electric Drive Motor & VFD Inverter

A3.name: Flush lubrication system and change oil

A7.name: Inspect spindle drive motor and inverter VFD

A8.name: Service heat exchanger and flush spindle coolant jacket

A9.name: De-rate cutting feed rate and re-calculate tool engagement

rules.why: Noise and vibration together are the primary acoustic and dynamic indicators of rolling element bearing wear.
Co-occurrence of extreme thermal rise, severe vibration, and abnormal acoustic emission indicates imminent spindle bearing seizure.
Thermal elevation and noise without severe high-amplitude vibration typically indicates lubricant starvation in raceways.
Ferrous debris detected in lubricant circulation alongside vibration signifies raceway spalling and particulate contamination.
Deteriorated workpiece surface roughness combined with synchronous vibration indicates angular or parallel spindle misalignment.
Elevated motor current draw paired with localized temperature increase suggests excessive frictional drag from deteriorating bearings.
A seized bearing represents catastrophic failure requiring complete bearing replacement to prevent permanent spindle shaft damage.
Significantly worn bearings must be scheduled for replacement before complete dimensional tolerance loss.
Replenishing grease/oil and clearing lubrication metering blocks resolves starvation faults.
Contaminated lubricant must be completely flushed and filtered to prevent rapid abrasive erosion of replacement components.
Spindle shaft runout and housing alignment must be precision calibrated using dial test indicators.
As an immediate interim measure, de-rating cutting load extends remaining useful life until planned maintenance downtime.

rules.then_safety: CRITICAL EMERGENCY STOP: Spindle bearing seizure detected. Halt spindle rotation immediately to prevent catastrophic rotor-stator lockup.
rules.why: Continuing operation with a seized bearing will cause permanent thermal deformation of the spindle housing and motor burnout.
Heat dissipation failure (HDF) occurs when process-to-air temperature differential delta_T < 8.6 K and spindle rotational speed < 1380 rpm (Matzka IEEE 2020).
Power failure (PWF) occurs when mechanical drive power P = Torque * angular_velocity falls below 3500 W or exceeds 9000 W (Matzka IEEE 2020).
Overstrain failure (OSF) occurs when the cumulative product of tool wear and cutting torque exceeds the variant threshold (11,000 for L, 12,000 for M, 13,000 for H) (Matzka IEEE 2020).
Tool wear failure (TWF) zone reached: tool accumulated cutting duration has entered the 200-240 minute critical wear-out window (Matzka IEEE 2020).
Random process failure (RNF) detected: uncorrelated electrical transient or sensor glitch identified outside nominal physical failure envelopes.
Heat dissipation failure requires immediate cleaning of the heat exchanger, inspection of coolant flow rate, and purging the spindle jacket.
Power failure outside 3.5-9.0 kW envelope requires electrical inspection of the VFD inverter, current sensors, and motor stator windings.
Severe overstrain induces cutting tool fracture and plastic deformation; the tool insert must be replaced immediately.
Overstrain requires de-rating feed rate and spindle speed to avoid recurring workpiece overload.
Tool wear life limit reached (200-240 min); tool insert must be indexed or replaced to prevent dimensional inaccuracy.

rules.then_safety: ELECTRICAL SAFETY ALERT: Spindle drive power anomalous (underload stall or dangerous power surge). Switch off CNC feed drive.
rules.why: Extreme power deviations threaten motor drive circuitry and present electrical or projectile hazard.

rules.then_safety: HIGH MECHANICAL STRESS WARNING: Severe tool/spindle overstrain detected. Stop cutting cycle to prevent cutter explosion or spindle bent shaft.
rules.why: Torque-wear overload exceeds structural safety limits of the tool and machine assembly.
